title: Guard a mutable Date

blocks.text: A `java.util.Date` is **mutable**: anyone holding a reference can call `setTime` and change it. A class that keeps a `Date` it was handed, or hands out the `Date` it keeps, lets outside code change its state behind its back. Where the `Date` type cannot be replaced (an old API still uses it), the page's fix is a **defensive copy**.
Write `Booking`, which must keep its start moment no matter what callers do with their `Date` objects:

rows: keep the `Date` you passed in, call `setTime(0)` on it

cases.says: A booking reports the start moment it was created with.
Changing the Date passed to the constructor afterwards does not change the booking.
Changing a Date returned by getStart does not change the booking.

concepts: A java.util.Date can be changed by anyone holding it, so a class that keeps one copies it on the way in and on the way out.
